name: OPA2156 / OPA156 (TI 36 V ultra-low-noise CMOS rail-to-rail I/O precision; single OPA156 unconfirmed)
tagline: TI 36 V CMOS rail-to-rail I/O precision dual: 3 nV/rtHz, 25 MHz, 40 V/us, ±25 uV. A few diyAudio posts rate its distortion alongside the OPA1656.
technology: CMOS-input precision op amp. The TI document title calls it 'CMOS' and DigiKey's product highlight says 'CMOS precision rail-to-rail'. It runs on 36 V total supply with rail-to-rail input and output and a 100 mA output drive. TI describes the OPA2156 as 'the first in a planned new generation of 36-V, rail-to-rail operational amplifiers'. As indexed, the datasheet title is 'OPA2156 36-V, Ultra-Low Noise, Wide-Bandwidth, Precision Rail-to-Rail Operational Amplifier'. It is not an audio-branded (Burr-Brown/SoundPlus) part.

reputation.summary: Praise is thin, and it is attributed forum comment rather than measurement. In the diyAudio thread 'OPA1656: High-Performance CMOS Audio Op Amp', posters said the OPA2156 has 'amazingly good distortion' and looks better than the OPA1656 in certain respects. No ASR or other published measurements were found. On GitHub it shows up mostly in instrumentation (a patch-clamp amplifier and a DAQ board, where the covg_clamp BOM lists OPA1656ID as the alternate) and in one DIY audio preamp output stage (bengineer91/Preamp). The discovery note calls it a 'higher-rail alternative to the OPA1656', which is wrong. Both are 36 V parts. What the OPA2156 adds is rail-to-rail input, precision offset (±25 uV) and 100 mA drive.
typical_uses: Precision / instrumentation front ends (patch-clamp amplifier, DAQ)
DIY audio preamp output/buffer stage (one GitHub project)
Candidate in place of OPA1656-class duals where rail-to-rail input, low offset or 100 mA drive is wanted
caveats: Not an audio-branded part. No audio THD+N measurements were found.
Only SMD packages (SOIC-8, VSSOP-8), so DIP socket rolling needs an adapter
Same 36 V supply limit as the OPA1656 (no supply-headroom advantage)
The praise is a handful of forum remarks. Tier C rests mostly on specs.

revision_history.changes: Initial release, dated from the 'SEPTEMBER 2018' first-publication date in the A and B headers. Contents and status (preview vs production data) not seen.
Revision confirmed via search (Sep 2018 - revised Dec 2018). Change log not retrieved. Chinese counterpart: ZHCSIQ3A (Dec 2018).
Latest revision seen as of September 2026, served by the ti.com symlink. Change log not retrieved. Chinese counterpart: ZHCSIQ3B (June 2019).
The revision and its date appear in a search summary. The changes were not shown.
The original release is inferred from the 'September 2018' first-publication date printed on Revs A and B. No copy of it was located.

Change log entry 'Changes from Original (September 2018) to Revision A': first release of the production-data data sheet. This means the original September 2018 SBOS900 was a pre-production (Product Preview / Advance Information) edition. Source: change log in the SBOS900B datasheet at ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2156.pdf.

Change log entry 'Changes from Revision A (December 2018) to Revision B': (1) added the DGK (VSSOP) package and its content; (2) extended Figure 8 (input voltage noise spectral density) to 10 MHz; (3) retitled the input bias and offset current curves (Figures 12 to 14) to state that they show SOIC package performance. So the Original and Rev A editions covered only the 8-pin SOIC (D). Source: ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2156.pdf.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found. It is a modern SMD-only TI part (SOIC-8/VSSOP-8) without the cult following that drives relabeling of DIP audio op-amps, so risk is presumably low. Buy from authorized distribution. alldatasheet gives the OPA2156ID top marking as 'OP2156'. Watch for the part-number collision: 'OPA156' hits on digchip and datasheetarchive point to an unrelated JFET-input op-amp document, not a single version of this TI CMOS part.
alternatives: OPA1656 / OPA1655 (TI Burr-Brown audio CMOS; 4.5-36 V; rail-to-rail output only; 2.9 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, 53 MHz GBW, 24 V/us, 3.9 mA/ch per SBOS901C). Pin-compatible SOIC-8 dual, listed as the OPA2156IDR alternate in the covg_clamp BOM.
OPA1688 (listed as the second alternate to OPA2156IDR in the covg_clamp BOM)
OPA828 / OPA2828 (TI JFET-input low-noise 36 V precision)
open_questions: Does the single OPA156 exist? No TI product page or orderable code was found, and the indexed datasheet title names only OPA2156.
SBOS900 change logs for A (Dec 2018) and B (June 2019) were not retrieved. Was the original Sept 2018 issue a Product Preview?
Which alldatasheet copy (1082239 vs 1154466) holds rev A and which holds rev B? The DigiKey HTML and datasheet4u copies have unknown revisions.
Datasheet quiescent current per channel, supply minimum, current noise and THD+N were not retrieved. The 4.4 mA covg_clamp figure is ambiguous.
No PCN or silicon-change information found. The TI PCN database was not searched directly.
Identity of the legacy 'OPA156 JFET Input Operational Amplifiers' document on digchip/datasheetarchive is unconfirmed.
Whether OPA2156 and OPA165x share a process platform: the consecutive literature numbers SBOS900/SBOS901 are the only hint.

revision_chain_notes: Texas Instruments SBOS900 (sole vendor, no second sources). Chain from oldest to newest: (1) SBOS900, original edition, September 2018. It was a pre-production (Product Preview / Advance Information) edition, SOIC only. This is inferred from the Rev A change-log line 'First release of production-data data sheet'. No copy found; MISSING. (2) SBOS900A, September 2018, revised December 2018. First production-data edition, still SOIC-only. The only copy is the low-confidence alldatasheet.com ID 1082239 entry already listed; no vendor or distributor copy confirmed; MISSING a confirmed copy. (3) SBOS900B, September 2018, revised June 2019. Added the DGK VSSOP package, extended the noise plot to 10 MHz and marked the Ib/Ios curves as SOIC data. Served by the ti.com symlink. Still current: none of the 4 searches found an SBOS900C. The Chinese edition, ZHCSIQ3, follows the same letters (original, A December 2018, B June 2019); only B is confirmed at ti.com.cn, and copies of the ZHCSIQ3 original and A are MISSING. New copies added: a Digi-Key France htmldatasheet and an alldatasheet.net OPA2156IDR page, both with revision not shown. The Wayback seeds are the ti.com symlink/gpn URLs: captures from September to December 2018 should hold the original preview, and captures from December 2018 to June 2019 should hold Rev A. Digi-Key PCN20240701000 and PCN20240902002 turned up in the searches but cover OPAx241/OPAx251 and OPAx134 (SBOS058A to B), not the OPA2156. No evidence of a silicon change under the part number; the only product change on record is the added VSSOP package in Rev B. The single OPA156 was not found in any result. Sources: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2156.pdf, https://www.digikey.fr/htmldatasheets/production/5061362/0/0/1/opa2156.pdf, https://www.alldatasheet.net/html-marking/1154469/TI1/OPA2156IDR/1289/18/OPA2156IDR.html, https://www.mouser.com/new/texas-instruments/ti-opa2156-op-amp/, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/6347/PCN20240701000.0.pdf, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/6370/PCN20240902002.1.pdf
